newsitem.title: USA: GM says may face strike at assembly plant.
newsitem.headline: GM says may face strike at assembly plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp.'s Moraine, Ohio, assembly plant has received notice from a union that it may strike the plant if a new contract is not reached by midnight next Monday, a GM spokesman said Tuesday.
"We're confident we can reach an agreement without a strike," said Jeff Kuhlman at GM's truck group headquarters in Pontiac, Mich.

The International Union of Electronic Workers Local 801 represents about 4,100 workers at the plant near Dayton, which assembles Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada sport/utility vehicles, Kuhlman said.
He declined to discuss the issues.
Kuhlman said that while the strike notification expires at one minute past midnight Monday, it could be extended if progress is made.
A union spokesman could not immediately be reached for comment.
Kuhlman said the Moraine plant is the lead GM plant for the vehicles it produces, assembling 289,000 in 1996.
